[[File:Warren Holland 2025 Worlds Special.png|thumb|right|260px|Warren Holland in the 2025 SWCCG Worlds Special]]
'''Warren Holland''' is the founder and CEO of [[Decipher|Decipher, Inc.]] Wikipedia's ''Star Wars'' Customizable Card Game article lists him among the game's designers with [[Tom Braunlich]], [[Rollie Tesh]], and [[Jerry Darcy]].<ref name="wp-decipher">[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Decipher,_Inc. Decipher, Inc.], Wikipedia</ref><ref name="wp-swccg">[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star_Wars_Customizable_Card_Game Star Wars Customizable Card Game], Wikipedia (designer credit line)</ref>

In a 2025 Worlds Special interview posted 14 June 2026, Holland told [[Brandon Baity]] how Decipher was founded and how the company obtained the ''Star Wars'' CCG license.<ref name="worlds-special">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BuZYhkg35qo 2025 SWCCG Worlds Special], brandon baity (NanashiStudios) (14 June 2026). Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-BuZYhkg35qo Internet Archive].</ref>

== Decipher founder ==

Holland identifies himself in that interview as CEO of Decipher. He traces the company to a Virginia Tech master's project inspired by a ''Smithsonian'' magazine article on the Beale ciphers. The first product was a puzzle with a $100,000 prize, sold at 50 cents each, with prize insurance through Lloyd's of London.<ref name="worlds-special" />

Wikipedia identifies Holland as founder of Decipher (1983, Norfolk, Virginia area) and a key executive alongside Cindy Thornburg.<ref name="wp-decipher" /> Decipher published SWCCG from December 1995 through 2001 after earlier success with ''Star Trek: The Next Generation'' CCG.<ref name="wp-decipher" /><ref name="wp-swccg" />

== Star Wars license and production ==

Holland said Decipher's path into licensed games ran through Pente Games to Parker Brothers, where he met [[Tom Braunlich]] and [[Rollie Tesh]]. The company took a ''Star Wars'' license and a side license with Parker Brothers for a two-player game. The first guarantee he names is $1 million.<ref name="worlds-special" />

For card images, Decipher had access to Lucas archives and a duplicate 70mm print of the original trilogy. Holland hired a German film editor (he names an $80,000 figure) for frame-by-frame high-resolution scans. He said a later Lucas encyclopedia used about one-third of Decipher's images. Work at Skywalker Ranch included being one of two licenses allowed to take the Episode I script off the ranch. For Special Edition characters who were not in the original film, Decipher hired a local theater company and actors.<ref name="worlds-special" />

Holland's interest in Joseph Campbell's hero's journey led to the game's split into Light Side and Dark Side.<ref name="bp-campbell">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AXdIdJwnjgc&t=535s The Booster Pack #28 — The making of the Star Wars CCG with Tom Braunlich], The Booster Pack Network (24 August 2022), 8:55–10:00. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261009/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AXdIdJwnjgc Internet Archive]. Transcript: [[The Booster Pack/Episode 28 transcript]].</ref> Through 1995 he reviewed every proposed card in the design team's evening sessions and passed none he did not love.<ref name="bp-sessions">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AXdIdJwnjgc&t=1283s The Booster Pack #28 — The making of the Star Wars CCG with Tom Braunlich], The Booster Pack Network (24 August 2022), 21:23–23:57. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261009/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AXdIdJwnjgc Internet Archive]. Transcript: [[The Booster Pack/Episode 28 transcript]].</ref>

The GeoCities anagram table maps Sandcrawler lore ("Warren-like") to Warren Holland, CEO of Decipher.<ref name="ana">[https://www.geocities.ws/plarathas/anagrams.html Anagramed Decipherians]</ref>

== Players' Committee announcement ==

In January 2002, Decipher CEO Warren Holland announced formation of a Players' Committee / player-advocate structure so fans could continue organized play and virtual support after the license ended.<ref name="wp-swccg" /><ref name="pc-hist">[[History of the Players Committee]]</ref> Holland's 25 January 2002 announcement named the first six Player Advocates (several already [[Squadron Members]]).<ref name="pc-adv">[https://web.archive.org/web/20160117001353/http://decipher.ruddog.com/starwars/playerscommittee1.html The Star Wars Players' Committee], 25 January 2002 (Wayback / ruddog)</ref>

The Ringer's 2018 feature interviews Holland about losing the Lucasfilm license and forming that player-advocate structure.<ref name="ringer">[https://www.theringer.com/2018/05/21/star-wars/star-wars-customizable-card-game-player-community The Force Is Strong With This ''Star Wars'' Subculture], The Ringer, 21 May 2018</ref>

== Interviews ==

=== Staff recollections ===
[[Bill Martinson]] said on ''[[Radio Free Decipher]]'' in April 1999 that [[Young Jedi]] was Holland's conception. Holland was closely involved in its gameplay and card design, and joked about his own "unreasonable standard of excellence".<ref>[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XvKFYzu0P-k&t=51s Broadcast 13 - Radio Free Decipher (09 April, 1999): Bill Martinson, Jerry Darcy on PD (Part 2)], Player's Council, YouTube (uploaded 20 February 2022), at 00:51. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-XvKFYzu0P-k Internet Archive]. Transcript: [[Radio Free Decipher/Episode 13 transcript]].</ref> Former staffer [[Jason Winter]] recalled in 2025 that Holland sat in on design meetings and preferred balancing cards through design rather than banned lists or copy limits. Holland also bought a house near the office for product development.<ref>[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=aq_dwh8Ojys&t=1091s Inside the Star Wars CCG: Secrets from Decipher], Imperial Remnant, YouTube (23 November 2025), at 18:11. Transcript: [[Inside the Star Wars CCG: Secrets from Decipher (transcript)]].</ref>

=== WARS Radio, July 2004 ===
In two July 2004 episodes of Decipher ''[[WARS Radio]]'' hosted by [[Mark Tuttle]], Holland explained why the ''Star Wars'' CCG mechanics returned in [[WARS TCG]], an original science-fiction property. He said a sci-fi setting with movement in space was "almost dictated" by the mechanics, and that building the universe around the game made for stronger science fiction.<ref>[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lxL-5bskkaw&t=185s Ep. 3 - Decipher WARS Radio (09 July, 2004): Warren Holland Interview; What's Happening in Art], Player's Council, YouTube (uploaded 15 May 2022), at 03:05. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-lxL-5bskkaw Internet Archive]. Transcript: [[WARS Radio/Episode 3 transcript]].</ref> He chose the name "Mumon Rift" from the Zen text ''The Gateless Gate''.<ref>[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lxL-5bskkaw&t=459s Ep. 3 - Decipher WARS Radio (09 July, 2004): Warren Holland Interview; What's Happening in Art], Player's Council, YouTube (uploaded 15 May 2022), at 07:39. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-lxL-5bskkaw Internet Archive]. Transcript: [[WARS Radio/Episode 3 transcript]].</ref> He described the five factions and said Gongen was the one he would live in.<ref>[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=FWBYRjMvhZw&t=569s Ep. 4 - Decipher WARS Radio (16 July, 2004): Holland Interview Part 2 and a Gongen Big Reveal!], Player's Council, YouTube (uploaded 15 May 2022), at 09:29. Transcript: [[WARS Radio/Episode 4 transcript]].</ref> Transcripts: [[WARS Radio/Episode 3 transcript|Episode 3]], [[WARS Radio/Episode 4 transcript|Episode 4]].

=== Radio Free Decipher, 5 October 2001 ===
After cancelling DecipherCon 2001, Holland went on ''[[Radio Free Decipher]]'' Broadcast 99 to answer players' questions. He said safety was the only reason for the decision. He compared the convention to a party on a barge offshore after shark sightings: most swimmers would be safe, but the company should not ask everyone to swim out.<ref>[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wS84wdG4EUI&t=242s Broadcast 99 - Radio Free Decipher (05 October, 2001): Warren Holland on DecipherCon and 9/11], Player's Council, YouTube (uploaded 13 May 2022), at 04:02. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-wS84wdG4EUI Internet Archive]. Transcript: [[Radio Free Decipher/Episode 99 transcript]].</ref> He said he had personally answered about 50 emails at ceo@decipher.com and that the qualified players would choose charities for the prize money.<ref>[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wS84wdG4EUI&t=49s Broadcast 99 - Radio Free Decipher (05 October, 2001): Warren Holland on DecipherCon and 9/11], Player's Council, YouTube (uploaded 13 May 2022), at 00:49. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-wS84wdG4EUI Internet Archive]. Transcript: [[Radio Free Decipher/Episode 99 transcript]].</ref>

=== Radio Free Decipher special broadcast, 28 December 2001 ===
In a ''[[Radio Free Decipher]]'' special broadcast with [[Kyle Heuer]], Holland announced that Lucasfilm would not renew Decipher's ''Star Wars'' CCG license. Sell-off ran through 30 April 2002.<ref>[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZpXfkPyurfE&t=3s Radio Free Decipher Special Broadcast (28 December, 2001): Warren Holland and the Players Committee], Player's Council, YouTube (uploaded 18 February 2022), at 00:03. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-ZpXfkPyurfE Internet Archive]. Transcript: [[Radio Free Decipher/Special Broadcast (28 December 2001) transcript]].</ref> He said the relationship with Lucasfilm had been good until Hasbro bought Wizards of the Coast. He had recently settled legal issues with Lucasfilm over its handling of the license.<ref>[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZpXfkPyurfE&t=183s Radio Free Decipher Special Broadcast (28 December, 2001): Warren Holland and the Players Committee], Player's Council, YouTube (uploaded 18 February 2022), at 03:03. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-ZpXfkPyurfE Internet Archive]. Transcript: [[Radio Free Decipher/Special Broadcast (28 December 2001) transcript]].</ref> He called Decipher's offer to keep the license the largest it had made for any license. Hasbro, he said, had convinced Lucasfilm it could double sales with a younger, ''Pokémon''-style audience.<ref>[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZpXfkPyurfE&t=282s Radio Free Decipher Special Broadcast (28 December, 2001): Warren Holland and the Players Committee], Player's Council, YouTube (uploaded 18 February 2022), at 04:42. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-ZpXfkPyurfE Internet Archive]. Transcript: [[Radio Free Decipher/Special Broadcast (28 December 2001) transcript]].</ref> He said ''Star Wars'' Second Edition and digital cards would have launched in 2001 had Lucasfilm approved them.<ref>[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZpXfkPyurfE&t=756s Radio Free Decipher Special Broadcast (28 December, 2001): Warren Holland and the Players Committee], Player's Council, YouTube (uploaded 18 February 2022), at 12:36. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-ZpXfkPyurfE Internet Archive]. Transcript: [[Radio Free Decipher/Special Broadcast (28 December 2001) transcript]].</ref> The cancellation of DecipherCon 2001, he said, had nothing to do with the license.<ref>[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZpXfkPyurfE&t=910s Radio Free Decipher Special Broadcast (28 December, 2001): Warren Holland and the Players Committee], Player's Council, YouTube (uploaded 18 February 2022), at 15:10. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-ZpXfkPyurfE Internet Archive]. Transcript: [[Radio Free Decipher/Special Broadcast (28 December 2001) transcript]].</ref> Decipher's first ''Lord of the Rings'' expansion had already outsold every SWCCG expansion of the previous four years.<ref>[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZpXfkPyurfE&t=1015s Radio Free Decipher Special Broadcast (28 December, 2001): Warren Holland and the Players Committee], Player's Council, YouTube (uploaded 18 February 2022), at 16:55. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-ZpXfkPyurfE Internet Archive]. Transcript: [[Radio Free Decipher/Special Broadcast (28 December 2001) transcript]].</ref> He then announced the [[Players Committee]].<ref name="rfd-sb-pc">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZpXfkPyurfE&t=1332s Radio Free Decipher Special Broadcast (28 December, 2001): Warren Holland and the Players Committee], Player's Council, YouTube (uploaded 18 February 2022), at 22:12. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-ZpXfkPyurfE Internet Archive]. Transcript: [[Radio Free Decipher/Special Broadcast (28 December 2001) transcript]].</ref>

=== NanashiStudios, 14 June 2026 ===
On-camera interview in ''2025 SWCCG Worlds Special'', posted by brandon baity (NanashiStudios). Holland speaks from about 3:05. The same video later reuses [[Chuck Kallenbach]] footage from ''May The 4th Be With Chuck''.<ref name="worlds-special" />

== Jedi Knights TCG ==
Holland is credited on Decipher's [[Jedi Knights Trading Card Game]] team. According to designer [[Chuck Kallenbach]], Holland asked him and [[Tom Lischke]] to "do something different" with the planned classic-trilogy version of [[Young Jedi]], which became Jedi Knights.<ref name="jkrules">[http://www.decipher.com/jediknights/rules/jediknightsrules.txt ''Jedi Knights'' Trading Card Game rulebook (credits)], Decipher (2001). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20010820125115/http://www.decipher.com:80/jediknights/rules/jediknightsrules.txt Internet Archive]</ref><ref name="tfnck">Josh Radke, [http://www.theforce.net/ccg/flashback/article.asp Flashback: Chuck Kallenbach interview], TheForce.Net. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261010072858/http://www.theforce.net/ccg/flashback/article.asp Internet Archive]</ref>
